changes.before: Return a frozen outer object with own version=1 (enumerable, non-writable, non-configurable) and theme={dark:false}. The nested theme remains mutable. No deep-freeze claim.
changes.after: Protect an object's own settings while understanding what stays changeable.

before: Object.defineProperty(object,name,descriptor) defines an own property and returns that same object. A data descriptor supplies value plus writable, enumerable and configurable flags. Here version is visible to ordinary own-key enumeration, but cannot be assigned a new value or deleted/reconfigured. Omitted flags default to false for a newly defined property.

Object.freeze(object) returns that same object after preventing new own properties and making its own data properties non-writable and non-configurable. It does not recursively freeze a nested object. In this lesson theme still refers to a mutable inner object. A const binding alone would not apply these property restrictions.

Implement the outer frozen settings object while keeping the nested theme object unfrozen. Optional practice: explain why replacing settings.theme and editing settings.theme.dark are different operations.
after:
A property descriptor sets rules for a property. `Object.defineProperty` uses those rules to create or change an own property.

`value` is the stored value. `writable` says whether it can be assigned a new value. `enumerable` says whether it appears in ordinary property listings. `configurable` says whether it can be deleted or its rules changed.

For our version property, only `enumerable` is true.

`Object.freeze(settings)` prevents adding or removing the object's own properties. Its own data properties cannot be assigned new values.

Freezing is shallow: it does not also freeze objects stored inside. Our nested `theme` object can still change. Declaring a variable with `const` alone would not freeze either object.

Complete `makeSettings()`. Give it `version: 1` and `theme: {dark: false}`. Make version visible in property listings, but not writable or configurable. Freeze the outer object.

Leave the inner theme object unfrozen. Replacing `settings.theme` changes an outer property, while editing `settings.theme.dark` changes an inner property.
